prompt: We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained networking environment for testing purposes. The infrastructure must include a VPC with a CIDR block of 10.0.0.0/16, containing a public subnet with a CIDR block of 10.0.1.0/24 and a private subnet with a CIDR block of 10.0.2.0/24. To enable external connectivity, attach an internet gateway to the VPC and configure a public route table associated with the public subnet that routes all outbound IPv4 (0.0.0.0/0) and IPv6 (::/0) traffic directly to the internet gateway.

We need a Terraform template that creates an IAM user named "TJ" with a custom IAM policy named "GlacierEFSEC2" attached, granting a broad set of EC2 management permissions along with EFS client-mount access and Glacier vault and multipart-upload permissions.

We need a Terraform template that creates a feature-complete Amazon S3 bucket module supporting dynamic naming, encryption, website hosting, access control, lifecycle management, CORS, logging, replication, and object lock configurations. The bucket name must derive from an optional bucket_name variable, falling back to "corebucket-" appended with a 4-byte random hexadecimal string if null, and appending an extra random string suffix when a boolean prefix variable is true. Key parameters must default as follows: request_payer to "BucketOwner", encryption to true, kms_key to an empty string (in which case the module creates its own rotating customer-managed KMS key, so encryption is always "aws:kms" with either the supplied key ARN or the module-created key), versioning, mfa_delete, force_destroy, and prefix to false, always blocking all public access on the bucket, while allowing optional overrides for ACLs, JSON policy documents, grants, tags, transfer acceleration status, logging target bucket and prefix, website index/error documents or redirect-all rules, CORS rules, lifecycle rules, and object lock configurations (supporting compliance/governance default retention modes and periods). Additionally, when replication_rules are supplied, the module must configure cross-region replication rules; if no external replication_role ARN is provided, it must automatically create a dedicated IAM role named "CoreS3ReplicationRole_" followed by the resolved bucket name assumed by "s3.amazonaws.com" with a custom policy "CoreS3ReplicationPolicy_" followed by the resolved bucket name permitting bucket list/replication actions and attach it directly to the role.

We need a Terraform template that creates an internal Application Load Balancer setup for testing path-based routing in a self-contained network. The infrastructure must be provisioned within a VPC having the CIDR block "10.0.0.0/16" and two subnets distributed across the first two available availability zones in the region using calculated /24 CIDR blocks. Deploy an internal Application Load Balancer that drops invalid header fields, using a security group that allows all ingress and egress traffic within the VPC CIDR, an HTTP target group on port 8080 configured with an HTTP health check on port 8081 at path "/health" (with an interval of 60 seconds, a timeout of 3 seconds, a matcher of "200-299", and healthy/unhealthy thresholds of 3), and an HTTPS listener on port 443 (TLS 1.3 security policy, self-signed certificate imported into ACM) forwarding to the target group. Additionally, create a configurable number of listener rules (governed by a resource count variable defaulting to 1) that forward traffic matching the path pattern "/static-N/*" (where N is the rule index, starting at 0) to the target group, starting at priority 100. All named resources must default to using the resource name "benchmark", and the region variable must default to "us-east-1".

We need a Terraform template that creates an AWS Backup vault infrastructure supporting multi-account patterns with customizable retention locking, SNS notifications, and workload-specific backup plans. The configuration must accept a required backup name variable, an account_type variable defaulting to "workload" (validated strictly to "workload" or "backup"), an optional KMS key ARN for vault encryption, and an optional vault policy string. When a min_retention_days parameter is provided, the template must configure a vault lock with optional max_retention_days and changeable_for_days. Optional vault notifications must be controlled by a boolean flag enable_aws_backup_vault_notifications (defaulting to false) to route failure events (defaulting to "BACKUP_JOB_FAILED" and "COPY_JOB_FAILED") to a specified SNS topic ARN. When account_type is set to "workload", the template must provision an IAM role prefixed with "aws-backup-" with the AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup managed policy attached, a backup plan named by combining "plan-" with the backup name value and the suffix "-backup", with configurable rule schedule, 60-minute start window, 120-minute completion window, cold storage transition after 30 days, deletion after 120 days, recovery point tagging, and dynamic cross-region or cross-account copy actions, alongside a tag-based backup selection matching key "Backup" equal to "true" using "STRINGEQUALS" and an additional resource-based selection if explicit ARNs are supplied in selection_resources.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained, serverless deployment of n8n automation on AWS ECS Fargate with persistent EFS storage and an internal Application Load Balancer. The stack must build a VPC using CIDR "10.0.0.0/16" across the first three availability zones with three private subnets ("10.0.0.0/24", "10.0.1.0/24", "10.0.2.0/24") and three public subnets ("10.0.4.0/24", "10.0.5.0/24", "10.0.6.0/24"), with no NAT or VPN gateways. Configurable variables must include a resource prefix defaulting to "n8n", an optional certificate_arn defaulting to null, an optional url override defaulting to null, a desired_count defaulting to 1, a container_image defaulting to "n8nio/n8n:1.4.0", and a fargate_type defaulting to "FARGATE_SPOT". The internal Application Load Balancer must be placed in the public subnets, drop invalid header fields, and use a security group allowing inbound HTTP (port 80) and HTTPS (port 443) from anywhere, forwarding traffic to an IP target group on port 80 with a 30-second deregistration delay and a health check path of "/healthz" (2 healthy/unhealthy threshold, 3-second timeout, 30-second interval). An HTTPS listener on port 443 using "ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06" must always be created, using certificate_arn when provided and otherwise a self-signed certificate generated in the stack and imported into ACM, while the HTTP listener on port 80 redirects to HTTPS. An encrypted EFS file system must be provisioned with an access point rooted at "/n8n" (owner UID/GID 1000, 777 permissions) and mount targets in the private subnets, restricted to NFS port 2049 from the VPC CIDR. An ECS cluster with container insights disabled must use the chosen Fargate capacity provider with base 1 and weight 100 and run a service that places tasks in the public subnets with public IP assignment enabled and a security group allowing port 5678 only from the load balancer. The Fargate task definition must use 256 CPU and 512 memory, mount the EFS volume with transit encryption and IAM authorization to "/home/node/.n8n", and run an essential container on port 5678 that logs through the awslogs driver to a CloudWatch log group named with the prefix followed by "-logs" with 1-day retention, setting N8N_SKIP_WEBHOOK_DEREGISTRATION_SHUTDOWN to "true" and WEBHOOK_URL to the url variable or otherwise the HTTPS load balancer endpoint. All security groups must limit outbound traffic to the VPC CIDR. Finally, create task and execution IAM roles assumable by "ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com", each with an inline policy permitting CloudWatch log group and stream operations.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained multi-tier network for hosting web applications, game servers, build sandboxes, and database services. The stack should create a VPC named "main" with CIDR block "10.0.0.0/16" and DNS support and DNS hostnames enabled, an internet gateway named "ig", DHCP options that set the internal domain name (defaulting to "internal") and DNS resolvers defaulting to the VPC's built-in resolver plus a standard public DNS server, and a private Route 53 hosted zone for that internal domain associated with the VPC. Provision five subnets, none of which auto-assign public IP addresses on launch, each with its own route table sending internet-bound traffic to the internet gateway: "reserved" ("10.0.0.0/24"), "sandbox" ("10.0.1.0/24"), "web" ("10.0.2.0/24"), "database" ("10.0.3.0/24"), and "gameserver" ("10.0.4.0/22"). Attach dedicated network ACLs to the sandbox, web, database, and gameserver subnets: the sandbox ACL allows all TCP in and out; the web ACL allows inbound TCP for SSH, HTTP, HTTPS, and ephemeral ports 32768-65535 and all outbound TCP; the database ACL only allows TCP to and from the web and gameserver subnet CIDRs; and the gameserver ACL allows inbound SSH, TCP and UDP on game ports 27015 and 27020, and TCP and UDP ephemeral ports 32768-65535, with all TCP and UDP allowed outbound. Finally, create a "Home SSH" security group allowing SSH from a configurable list of admin CIDRs (defaulting to the documentation range "203.0.113.0/24") and from itself, and a "Packer SSH" security group allowing SSH from the VPC CIDR and from itself, with both groups restricting outbound traffic to the VPC CIDR.

We need a Terraform template that creates a highly configurable, enterprise-grade Amazon S3 bucket architecture with advanced security controls, data protection policies, event notifications, and cross-region replication capabilities. The S3 bucket must accept an optional name (validated to 63 characters max) or name_prefix (validated to 37 characters max), force_destroy defaulting to false, object ownership defaulting to "BucketOwnerEnforced" (which conditionally provisions canned ACLs only when set to "ObjectWriter"), and public access block controls defaulting block_public_acls, block_public_policy, ignore_public_acls, and restrict_public_buckets to true. Server-side encryption must automatically default to AES256 unless a kms_key_arn is provided, which switches the algorithm to "aws:kms" and enables bucket keys, while bucket versioning defaults to "Suspended" unless enabled via a boolean flag. The bucket policy must combine any supplied custom JSON policy with an enforced SSL-only access policy (denying s3:* requests when "aws:SecureTransport" is false) and a conditional logging permissions policy allowing "logging.s3.amazonaws.com" to perform PutObject when logging_source_bucket_arns are specified. Additionally, the template must support optional EventBridge notifications, server access logging with preconditions preventing combined logging and object locking, object lock retention rules (mode, days, years) with preconditions against source bucket logging, multi-rule cross-region replication settings with priority keys and source selection criteria, inventory configurations targeting Parquet or SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encrypted destinations on a schedule, CORS configuration, and dynamic lifecycle management rules handling object expirations, transitions, noncurrent versions, and incomplete multipart upload aborts.

We need a Terraform template that creates a versatile AWS Transfer Family SFTP server solution supporting public or VPC-hosted endpoints, automated user provisioning, and optional Route 53 DNS mapping. The server identifier must derive from an explicit name variable or fallback to a two-word hyphenated random pet name, defaulting logging to a dynamically provisioned IAM role attached to "AWSTransferLoggingAccess" unless an explicit logging role ARN is provided. If configured for API Gateway authentication, the module must provision an API Gateway authorization IAM role with CloudWatch logging permissions. The server endpoint type must support "PUBLIC", "VPC", or "VPC_ENDPOINT" modes, defaulting to "PUBLIC" with "S3" storage and "SFTP" protocols, while supporting optional FTPS ACM certificates, custom login banners, custom security policies (defaulting to "TransferSecurityPolicy-2023-05"), host keys, structured CloudWatch log destinations, and protocol details for AS2, passive IP, set-stat options, or TLS session resumption. When hosted inside a VPC without pre-existing network resources supplied in endpoint details, it must automatically create a dedicated security group opening port 22 to 0.0.0.0/0 along with an Elastic IP per specified subnet. Furthermore, if a Route 53 hosted zone is specified, create a CNAME record mapping a sub-domain (defaulting to "sftp") to the Transfer Server endpoint. Finally, for each user in a map of SFTP users, provision an IAM role and policy granting list and object access to their specified S3 home directory bucket path, an AWS Transfer user, and associate any matching SSH public keys provided in a secondary user key map.

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-tier, dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 AWS network architecture to host a secure three-tier application environment. The stack must deploy a VPC tagged "main-vpc" with a default IPv4 CIDR block of "10.16.0.0/16", Amazon-provided IPv6 CIDR assignment enabled (controlled by is_ipv6_enabled defaulting to true), default instance tenancy, and both DNS hostnames and DNS support enabled by default. To calculate subnet allocations, the template must use the "hashicorp/subnets/cidr" module (version 1.0.0) to dynamically calculate IPv4 subnets using 4 additional bits (/20 subnets) and IPv6 subnets using 8 additional bits (/64 subnets) across a list of subnet objects (sn_details) containing subnet names, target availability zones, and public/private indicators, defaulting to 12 subnets across three availability zones for web (public), app (private), database (private), and reserved (private) tiers. An Internet Gateway tagged with a name prefixed by "main-igw-vpc-" followed by the VPC's resource ID must be attached to the VPC, and a public route table tagged "public-rt-web" routing all IPv4 ("0.0.0.0/0") and IPv6 ("::/0") traffic to the Internet Gateway must be created and associated exclusively with all subnets marked as public. Finally, security groups must be provisioned for each tier: a "web_sg" permitting ingress port 443 (TLS) from "0.0.0.0/0" and port 22 (SSH) only from the VPC IPv4 CIDR block and egress port 443 to "app_sg"; an "app_sg" permitting ingress port 443 from "web_sg" and egress port 443 to "db_sg"; and a "db_sg" permitting ingress port 443 from "app_sg".

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive, secure AWS CloudTrail logging architecture for auditing and compliance across account activities. The setup must provision a dedicated CloudTrail trail, an S3 log storage bucket, a CloudWatch Log Group, an IAM role for CloudWatch Logs ingestion, a KMS key for encryption, and an optional SNS notification topic. The S3 bucket name must default to dynamic generation incorporating account ID, region, and a random 8-character lowercase suffix if unspecified, with all public access blocked and default SSE-KMS encryption using the dedicated CloudTrail KMS key, featuring configurable force destroy (defaulting to true), versioning configuration (defaulting to false), and an S3 bucket policy permitting CloudTrail ACL checks and put-object actions with full control. CloudTrail log file encryption must use a dedicated KMS key with a 30-day deletion window, automated annual key rotation, an alias prefix, and a key policy granting permissions to root IAM users, CloudTrail encryption contexts, CloudWatch Logs, S3 bucket encryption, and an optional role ARN provided for log decryption. The CloudWatch Log Group must default to retaining logs for 90 days, populated by a dedicated IAM role and policy allowing CloudTrail to create log streams and put log events. CloudTrail itself must enforce log file validation, include global service events (defaulting to true), multi-region trails (defaulting to true), logging toggles (defaulting to true), organization trail toggles (defaulting to false), event selectors with configurable read/write types (defaulting to "All"), management events (defaulting to true), dynamic data resource selectors, and dynamic insight selectors. Finally, the module should support conditionally creating an SNS topic for alerts (disabled by default) with a topic policy allowing CloudTrail publishing, otherwise using an optional SNS topic ARN input that defaults to empty.

We need a Terraform template that creates a WebSocket API on Amazon API Gateway v2 that forwards client messages directly into an Amazon SQS queue without any Lambda functions. Use a randomly generated two-word pet name for both the API and the queue, encrypt the queue with a dedicated customer-managed KMS key with automatic rotation, and create an IAM execution role assumable by API Gateway with SQS access and CloudWatch Logs permissions. The connect route should use a mock integration that returns a 200 status code, the default route should send the raw message body to the queue through a SendMessage AWS service integration and return the integration response to the client, and the disconnect route should send a fixed "Client disconnected" message to the same queue. Deploy the API to an auto-deployed stage named "dev" with access logging to a CloudWatch log group under the /aws/apigateway/ prefix retained for one day, and output the full WebSocket endpoint URL including the stage name.

We need a Terraform template that creates an Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Point backed by two replicated buckets for highly available object storage. Provision a primary bucket in us-east-1 and a secondary bucket in the second region that AWS requires for Multi-Region Access Point control-plane operations (the access point and its policy must also be managed from that region), with bucket names taken from variables defaulting to "example1" and "example2" and suffixed with the AWS account ID. Each bucket needs versioning enabled, a private ACL with BucketOwnerPreferred object ownership, all public access blocked, and default SSE-KMS encryption using its own customer-managed KMS key with automatic rotation. Configure replication from the primary bucket to the secondary bucket for KMS-encrypted objects using the STANDARD storage class and the secondary key for replicas, using an IAM role assumable by S3 that grants the required read, replicate, decrypt, and encrypt permissions. Finally, create a Multi-Region Access Point named from a variable defaulting to "example-mrap" spanning both buckets, with an access point policy that allows only the owning account to get and put objects through it.

We need a Terraform template that creates a VPC named "projectvpc" with CIDR block "10.0.0.0/16" containing a public subnet "10.0.1.0/24" in the first availability zone of us-east-1 and a private subnet "10.0.2.0/24" in the second availability zone, where the public subnet routes to the internet through an Internet Gateway and the private subnet routes outbound traffic through a NAT gateway with an Elastic IP placed in the public subnet.

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure S3 bucket for endpoint backups named "endpoint-backup" followed by a hyphen and the current AWS account ID, with all public access blocked, transfer acceleration suspended, object lock disabled, and default server-side encryption using S3-managed keys (AES256). Attach a bucket policy that denies insecure requests not made over TLS 1.2 or higher and denies uploads or retention changes that would place objects in compliance-mode lock for more than 90 days. Also create an IAM user named "endpoint-backup" and a customer-managed IAM policy named "endpoint-backup-bucket-read-write-access" granting list, read, write, delete, version, retention, and restore access to this bucket and decrypt/data-key access on the AWS-managed S3 KMS key, attached to that user, without creating any access keys.
